definitions.gloss: bundling; selling items together as a set; tie-in sale
definitions.explanation: Selling a desirable item only together with a less popular one, or combining products as a set. In commerce, {抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせ{販売|はんばい} (tie-in selling) is a way to move slow stock and is sometimes viewed negatively.

examples.japanese: {人気|にんき}{商品|しょうひん}と{抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせで{売|う}られていた。
examples.english: It was sold bundled with a popular product.

examples.japanese: そのソフトは{別|べつ}のサービスとの{抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせだ。
examples.english: That software comes bundled with another service.

examples.japanese: {売|う}れ{残|のこ}りを{人気|にんき}{商品|しょうひん}との{抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせで{処分|しょぶん}しようとした。
examples.english: They tried to clear unsold stock by bundling it with a popular product.

notes:
From the verb {抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせる (to combine, make things go together). Most common in the phrase {抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせ{販売|はんばい} (tie-in sale).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせ{販売|はんばい}: tie-in sale; bundled selling
- {抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせで{売|う}る: to sell as a bundle
- チケットの{抱|だ}き{合|あ}わせ: bundled tickets
